visual.general_description: Colour flow diagram of the pathophysiology of chronic wounds in diabetic foot ulcers, with a small clinical photograph at top left.
visual.detailed_description: On a white background a colour photograph at top left shows the plantar side of a foot with a round ulcer with a pale rim, labelled "diabetic foot ulcer". A black arrow leads down to an orange-outlined box listing four items: repetitive tissue damage, detritus, bacterial toxins and diabetic neuropathy. A second arrow leads to a grey-outlined box reading "increased and prolonged inflammatoric reaction" and "immigration of granulocytes", which connects to a grey box "makrophages" with two grey ovals, "M1 subtype" and "M2 subtype". Coloured arrows from the ovals carry cytokine labels: orange for "INF γ", "IL-1β", "TNF α" and "MMP 9" and green for "IL-4", "TGF β" and "IL-10", with yellow arrows entering from "INF γ" and "IL-4". A double-headed black arrow joins the macrophage group to blue boxes "fibroblasts" and "keratinocytes" and to boxes reading "serin-proteases" with an up arrow, "MMP's" with an up arrow and "TIMP's" with a down arrow. An upward arrow leads to an orange box listing degradation of extracellular matrix, regeneration of tissue loss, increasing mitosis, keratinocyte's migration and angiogenesis, then to an orange box "Chronic inflammation leads to chronicity of wound", and a final thick arrow to a grey box "malignant transformation". A legend at bottom left shows orange "pro-inflammatory", green "anti-inflammatory" and yellow "stimlating" arrows.
